result.title: TextVBench: Evaluating Text Rendering and Preservation in Video Generation
result.summary: Modern video generators can synthesize convincing scenes while rendering a few characters incorrectly, omitting requested text, or changing it across frames. Measuring these failures is harder than applying OCR independently to each frame: when a scene contains multiple text targets and multiple noisy OCR regions, the evaluator must first determine which observation belongs to which intended text. We introduce TextVBench, a benchmark and evaluation framework that formulates visual-text evaluation as a multi-target, multi-instance spatiotemporal correspondence problem. TextVBench contains two complementary tracks: TextVBench-T2V measures the creation and maintenance of prompt-specified text, while TextVBench-Ref2V measures preservation of text from reference images. Both tracks use target-conditioned candidate selection rather than unconstrained VLM transcription, support one target mapping to multiple OCR regions, and separate frame-level spatial fidelity from cross-frame temporal fidelity. A length-weighted harmonic score summarizes these factors, while extra-text diagnostics expose failure modes hidden by a single OCR score. The benchmark is organized around controlled text, layout, carrier, and motion attributes so that aggregate scores can be traced back to specific capability limits. Across the evaluated model runs, MiniMax-H3 reaches a T2V TextVScore of 68.32, while the strongest Ref2V score is 56.51; attribute slices reveal a pronounced drop as the number of simultaneous reference text regions increases.

AI.brief_summary: TextVBench 提出一个评测视频生成中文本渲染与保持的基准与框架，把视觉-文本评测建模为多目标、多实例的时空对应问题，含 T2V 与 Ref2V 两条 track，并用长度加权调和分数区分帧内空间保真与跨帧时间一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是视频生成评测而非 VLM 推理，但「目标条件候选选择」而非无约束 VLM 转写、以及分离空间与时间保真度的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据归属、多种 latent 假设筛选与评价设计提供可核查线索。
